name: go-indep-4
requirements: semver/semver.go: Parse(s string) (Version, error) accepts exactly SemVer 2.0.0 syntax and returns an error for anything else: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH decimal numbers that fit in uint64, then an optional -prerelease and an optional +build, each a dot-separated list of nonempty identifiers made only of ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Core numbers and all-digit prerelease identifiers have no leading zeros (build identifiers may). Nothing may precede or follow the version, not even spaces. Pre and Build hold the identifiers in order. String() returns MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, then -Pre and +Build joined with dots when nonempty, so it round-trips every valid input. Compare(a, b) returns -1, 0 or 1 by SemVer precedence: core numbers numerically; a version with a prerelease ranks below the same version without one; prerelease identifiers compare left to right, all-digit ones numerically and below any others, others in ASCII byte order; if every shared identifier is equal, the longer list ranks higher. Build metadata never affects Compare. ParseConstraint(s string) (Constraint, error) parses alternatives separated by || (spaces around them allowed); an alternative is one or more comparators separated by spaces, all of which must hold. A comparator is an optional operator (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=, ~ or ^) immediately followed by a version that Parse accepts; no operator means =. Operators compare with Compare. ~X.Y.Z means >=X.Y.Z and <X.(Y+1).0. ^X.Y.Z means >=X.Y.Z and <(X+1).0.0, or <0.(Y+1).0 when X is 0, or <0.0.(Z+1) when X and Y are 0. Anything else, including an empty alternative, is an error. Check(v) reports whether any alternative holds, except that a version with a prerelease satisfies an alternative only if one of its comparators names a version with the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and a prerelease. Max(versions, c) returns the highest version that satisfies c, and false when none does. In a constraint, a hyphen range A - B (spaces around the hyphen, plain versions on both sides) is the two comparators >=A <=B. IncMajor, IncMinor and IncPatch return the next version with no prerelease or build: X+1.0.0, X.Y+1.0 and X.Y.Z+1, except that a prerelease already at that level is released instead: X.0.0-pre.IncMajor() is X.0.0, X.Y.0-pre.IncMinor() is X.Y.0, and X.Y.Z-pre.IncPatch() is X.Y.Z. Sort(versions) sorts by Compare and keeps the order of equal versions.

ini/ini.go: Parse(text string) (File, error). Lines are separated by \n, and spaces, tabs and \r are trimmed from both ends of every line. A line ending in a backslash continues: drop the backslash and join the trimmed text before it to the next trimmed line with one space, repeatedly; the joined line has the first line's number. Skip blank lines and lines starting with ; or # (there are no inline comments). A line starting with [ must end with ] and names a section (trimmed, nonempty); keys before any header belong to section "". Every other line is key = value, split at the first =, with the key (nonempty) and value trimmed. A value starting with a double quote must end at its closing quote: the quotes are removed, inner spaces kept, and \" and \\ are the only escapes. A repeated key replaces the earlier value, and a repeated header continues that section. Names are case-sensitive. The result has an entry for every header seen, even with no keys, and for section "" only when it has keys. Any other line, an empty name or key, a bad escape, an unterminated quote or text after the closing quote fails with a *Error whose Line is the 1-based line number. After parsing, values are interpolated: $$ becomes $, ${name} becomes the interpolated value of name in the same section, ${section:name} that of name in section (split at the first colon; ${:name} is section ""), and any other $ is kept. Forward references work, and a repeated key's last value is used. A reference to a missing key, an unclosed ${ or a cycle fails with a *Error whose Line is the assignment line of the first key, in line order, whose value cannot be interpolated. Get(section, key) returns a value and whether it exists. Bool accepts 1, true, yes, on, 0, false, no and off in any letter case; Int accepts what strconv.ParseInt(value, 0, 64) accepts; Duration accepts what time.ParseDuration accepts. Each returns an error for a missing key or any other value. Format(f File) string writes the keys of section "" first without a header, then every other section, even an empty one, as [name] in sorted order, each followed by its keys in sorted order as key = "value": every value is double-quoted with \" and \\ escaped and each $ doubled. Each line ends with \n and there are no blank lines, so Parse(Format(f)) equals f for any f that Parse returned. Sections() returns every section name in sorted order. List(section, key) splits the value at commas, trims spaces and tabs from each item and drops empty items; a missing key is an error.

textwrap/textwrap.go: Wrap(text string, width int) []string wraps greedily, counting runes, not bytes. Blank lines (only whitespace) separate paragraphs: leading and trailing blank lines are dropped, and consecutive paragraphs are separated by exactly one "" line. Within a paragraph, words are maximal runs of non-whitespace; whitespace, newlines included, only separates them. Each line takes as many words as fit, joined by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space. A word longer than width starts a new line and is cut into width-rune pieces; its last piece may be followed by more words. Text with no words gives no lines, and width < 1 counts as 1. Fill joins Wrap's lines with \n. Indent(text, prefix string) adds prefix to every line that contains non-whitespace; other lines and all newlines are unchanged. Dedent(text string) removes the longest run of spaces and tabs (compared byte for byte) that starts every line containing non-whitespace, and empties whitespace-only lines while keeping their newlines. Justify(text string, width int) []string returns Wrap's lines, but each line that is not the last of its paragraph and has two or more words is widened to exactly width runes by adding spaces between its words: gap sizes differ by at most one, and the leftmost gaps are the wider ones. Shorten(text string, width int, placeholder string) string collapses every whitespace run to one space and trims the ends; if the result has at most width runes it is returned. Otherwise it returns the most leading words, joined by spaces and followed directly by placeholder, that fit in width runes; if not even one word fits, it returns placeholder without its leading whitespace when that fits, else "". ExpandTabs(text string, tabSize int) string replaces each tab with spaces up to the next column that is a multiple of tabSize, counting columns in runes from the start of each line; tabSize < 1 counts as 1. WrapIndent(text string, width int, first, rest string) []string wraps like Wrap but starts each paragraph's first line with first and its other lines with rest; a prefix counts toward width, leaving at least 1 rune for words, and a long word's pieces fill each line's room. The "" lines between paragraphs get no prefix. Center(line string, width int) string pads line with spaces to width runes, half on each side with any odd space on the right; a line already at least width runes long is unchanged. Table(rows [][]string, gap int) []string aligns cells into left-aligned columns, each as wide in runes as its widest cell, separated by gap spaces (gap < 1 counts as 1); rows may have fewer cells, and trailing spaces are trimmed from every line. Box(text string, width int) []string frames Wrap(text, width-4): with inner the rune count of the longest wrapped line, the first and last lines are + then inner+2 dashes then +, and each wrapped line, blank ones included, becomes "| " + the line padded with spaces to inner runes + " |".

ratelimit/ratelimit.go: a token bucket. New(rate float64, burst int, clock Clock) starts full with burst tokens (burst < 0 counts as 0) and reads clock.Now(). Before every method the bucket earns rate tokens per second of clock time since its last reading, fractions included, capped at burst; rate <= 0 earns nothing, and a clock earlier than the last reading earns nothing and does not move the reading back. AllowN(n) takes n tokens and returns true if n is at most the tokens held; otherwise it takes nothing and returns false. n < 0 is always false, and AllowN(0) is always true. Allow is AllowN(1). Tokens returns the current, possibly fractional, count without taking any. Delay(n) returns 0 if AllowN(n) would succeed now; -1 if it never can (n < 0, n > burst, or too few tokens and rate <= 0); otherwise the wait until enough tokens are earned, rounded up to a whole nanosecond. SetRate earns at the old rate up to now, then switches rate. SetBurst earns up to now, then sets the size (negative counts as 0) and drops tokens above it; it adds none. Reserve(n int) *Reservation is refused (OK() false, Delay() -1, nothing taken) when n < 0, n > burst, or rate <= 0 and fewer than n tokens are held. Otherwise it takes n tokens at once, even below zero, and becomes ready after the wait Delay(n) would have returned just before; its Delay() is the time left until then, never below 0. Cancel() on a granted reservation, no later than its ready time, gives its n tokens back (capped at burst) once; otherwise, and on later calls, it does nothing. NewGroup(rate float64, burst int, clock Clock) *Group keeps one Limiter per key, created full on the key's first use; Group.AllowN(key, n) and Group.Allow(key) use that key's limiter. Len() counts keys with a limiter. Prune() removes every limiter that holds burst tokens and returns how many it removed. Group.Reserve(key, n) is Reserve(n) on that key's limiter, and Group.Tokens(key) reports its tokens, or burst (at least 0) for a key with no limiter, without creating one. NewWindow(limit int, period time.Duration, clock Clock) *Window is a sliding log: an event recorded at time t counts while the clock is before t + period. Allow() records an event at the current time and returns true if fewer than limit events count; otherwise it records nothing and returns false. Count() returns how many events count. Retry() returns 0 if Allow would succeed now, -1 if limit < 1, and otherwise the time until the earliest counted event stops counting. Group.SetRate and Group.SetBurst apply Limiter.SetRate and Limiter.SetBurst to every existing limiter and set the values used for limiters created later.

allocation.A: semver/semver.go and ini/ini.go, with focused tests.
allocation.B: textwrap/textwrap.go and ratelimit/ratelimit.go, with focused tests.
